text:
neel: Ran nsys on the fused-flash handoff path this morning. Seeing a KV-cache write spike (~3.2ms) in the write kernel when batch size transitions 8 -> 16. Timeline uploaded: https://perf.redwood/nsys/2456789012 :eyes:

tess: can you paste the exact nsys command and the short summary? also which model/seq_len?

neel: command I used:
```
nsys profile -o fused-handoff --trace=cuda,nvtx --sample=none --duration=60 \\n  -- ./runtime_server --model gpt-phi-8k --batcher-config batch_size=8:16 --seq_len=256
```
summary from nsys (top kernels):
- fused_attention_forward          0.82ms
- fused_attn_kv_write             3.21ms  <-- the spike
- kv_cache_host_memcpy            0.05ms
- fused_attn_backward             1.12ms

maria: interesting. that write time is too high for a 256 seq. did you capture sm occupancy / l2 stats? run with `--export-cupti=...` or use nvprof to get metrics: `sm__warps_active.avg.pct`, `l2_subp0_read_transactions`

ryan: my first guess is kernel-selector flip: when batcher jumps, selector may pick non-fused variant that does a different write pattern (more scattered writes or additional atomic ops). timeline often shows an extra memcpy/host-sync right after selector change. check nvtx markers around the handoff.

neel: good call. I do see an NVTX marker `batcher:hand-off` at 00:22:11 and then the write kernel starts. here's the timeline slice around the event (copied):
```
00:22:10.987  NVTX: batcher:hand-off
00:22:11.002  fused_attn_forward (0.80ms)
00:22:11.009  fused_attn_kv_write (3.21ms)  <-- long gap on SM timeline
00:22:11.013  kv_cache_host_memcpy (0.05ms)
```

tess: can you run two quick nsys captures: seq_len=256 with batch boundary at 8->8 (no handoff), and seq_len=256 with forced boundary 8->16 so we reproduce the exact selector path? also try `--capture-range=cudaProfilerApi` so we only get the critical region.

perf-bot: Automated regression detector: similar KV write increase observed in nightly 2026-03-16 at commit a1b2c3d -> a1b2c3f. Flagged as "kvcache-write-latency-regression".

maria: that regression commit touched kernel heuristics + fused-attn tiling. could be a change that widened the condition for fused->unfused fallback. if we have per-kernel shared memory usage before/after, we can compare occupancy. run `nvprof --metrics shared_load_transactions_per_request,sm_efficiency` on the smaller reproducer.

ryan: also check bank conflict patterns. last time we saw 3ms spikes it was due to smem aliasing when kvcache write buffer aligned on a bad stride. try running with `--smem-affinity=packed` in the debug runtime to see if spike disappears.

neel: will run the pairwise traces now (seq=256 stable, seq=256 handoff forced) and collect nvprof metrics + perfetto slice export. any specific perfetto slices to diff?

tess: capture `gpu/hardware/copy` and `cuda/kernels` slices plus `memory` rails. export with perfetto UI and do a small slice-diff between the two traces. if the write appears in different kernel variants, the shapes will be obvious.

maria: if you can upload both traces, I'll run a quick flamegraph diff tomorrow and check L2/DRAM traffic per-kernel. if it's a selector bug we should see the same kernel name but different register/shared mem usage, or different kernel name entirely.

neel: ack. I'll post traces & nvprof output here in an hour. adding @tess @maria for follow-up. thanks :thumbsup:
